patterns.usage_note: Path を marks the space a motion verb passes over or through — 道[みち]を歩[ある]く, 空[そら]を飛[と]ぶ, 橋[はし]を渡[わた]る, 角[かど]を曲[ま]がる — and is not the direct-object を, even though the form is identical; the verbs it pairs with are motion verbs that take no other object. Because Japanese resists two を in one clause, a path を and an object を rarely share a predicate. Where で would present the area as a venue (公園で走[はし]る, running around inside the park), を traces a route across it (公園を走る, running through and out the other side).

examples.ruby: 毎朝[まいあさ]この川沿[かわぞ]いの道[みち]を歩[ある]いている。
examples.english: Every morning I walk along this riverside path.

examples.ruby: 大[おお]きな鳥[とり]が校庭[こうてい]の上空[じょうくう]を横切[よこぎ]った。
examples.english: A large bird cut across the sky above the schoolyard.

examples.ruby: 子[こ]どもたちが橋[はし]を渡[わた]って学校[がっこう]へ向[む]かう。
examples.english: The children head off to school across the bridge.
